title: Directories and Pathnames
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of directories and pathnames in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply directories and pathnames in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to working with platform-independent paths and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Directories and Pathnames through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding directories and pathnames helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Directories and Pathnames helps you reason about file and directory checks. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: File and directory checks. Then connect it to Creating and enumerating directories. The remaining syllabus points—Working with platform-independent paths—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports directories and pathnames. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for directories and pathnames using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Working with platform-independent paths), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` in a folder where you may create files. The example removes notes.txt after reading it. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain directories and pathnames, identify its place in files, input/output, and the standard library, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
